data.text:
Tsunami alert issued after massive 8.8 quake in Russia and Japan 
 
Tsunamis swept parts of Russia’s Far East on Wednesday after a powerful 8.8-magnitude earthquake, prompting urgent evacuation orders and Pacific-wide tsunami alerts. Russian authorities confirmed flooding in Severo-Kurilsk, where 2,000 people were evacuated.
 
Japan issued alerts as far south as Osaka, with residents seen fleeing to higher ground.
 
The quake, upgraded from an initial 8.0 to 8.8 by the US Geological Survey, is the strongest in Kamchatka since 1952. It triggered six aftershocks and wave warnings across the Pacific — from Chile and Hawaii to the Philippines and California. Japan halted coastal trains and evacuated Fukushima nuclear workers as precautionary measures.
